Remember which level of protein structure gives you alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets, and which one is held together by hydrogen bonds between parts of the backbone.
walkthrough:
**Observe the diagram shape**

Look at the drawing of the spider silk chain. It is not a coil or spring shape. It is made of flat, zig-zag strands lying parallel and stacked together in crystalline blocks.

That stacked zig-zag pattern is the classic signature of beta-pleated sheets.

**Recall the levels of protein structure**

Primary structure is just the sequence of amino acids, like glycine-alanine-glycine-alanine. Secondary structure is the first level of folding, held by hydrogen bonds, and it has only two main forms: alpha-helices (coiled) and beta-pleated sheets (folded zig-zags).

**Put the two clues together**

The question tells you there are repeated glycine and alanine sequences (primary sequence), but the diagram shows how that chain is folded into stacked sheets. That folding is secondary structure, of the beta-pleated sheet type, which gives silk its great strength.

options.A: Primary structure is only the amino acid sequence. It does not include alpha-helices, which are a folded secondary structure, and the diagram shows sheets not coils.
options.B: Correct. The zig-zag stacked regions are beta-pleated sheets, which are a type of secondary structure held by hydrogen bonds.
options.C: Tertiary structure is the further 3D folding of a whole single polypeptide, and the diagram does not show alpha-helices (coils).
options.D: Quaternary structure needs two or more separate polypeptide chains joined together. Here we are shown folding within one spider silk polypeptide chain, so it is secondary not quaternary.
